title: The outside alarm has been red on every scheduled run since 2026-11-20 and the problems it names are real (backup failed, Mac on battery)
evidence: gh run list --workflow=server-alarm.yml, checked 2026-11-21 22:50Z: the last 7 scheduled runs (11-20 01:45Z through 11-21 21:38Z) all 'failure'; the 5 before them (11-18 12:57Z to 11-19 19:37Z) 'success'. Gaps between runs 5 to 9 hours, not 30 minutes. Log of run 44922705463 (11-21 16:06Z): 'WATCH FAILED 4 problem(s): mac_job_failed: The Mac job "backup" failed its last run. mac_job_stale: disk, integrity. mac_on_battery: The Mac is running on battery (80% left)'. Runs 44715034388 to 44881334452 list 1 to 3 problems each. The 11-21 21:38Z run: '28 of 28 routes work', then 'WATCH FAILED watch.ok is false and no problems are listed'. One live GET of /api/health at 22:50Z returned watch {"ok":false}. First failure 11-20 01:45Z was 'server error 530' (tunnel). So the alarm is firing daily with real content and nobody has cleared it in ~2 days: a person who gets a daily red email learns to ignore it, and a real outage looks the same as the standing red.
fix: Clear the standing problems (backup, disk and integrity jobs, plug the Mac in), then keep the alarm green so any red means act; add a second route that pages a phone (an uptime monitor on /api/health is already written up in needs-jamin.md near line 131) and have it page both founders.
fix_cost: 1 to 2 hours for the cleanup; uptime monitor free tier, 20 minutes
dup_of: R02 (late schedule known); new: red for 2 days, causes named, backup job failing, 11-20 530 outage

title: Apple developer account is one individual: one person holds seller name, renewal, payouts and every appeal
evidence: RULINGS.md:569-574: 'Apple account individual', order W1979673460, 'Enrolment Complete' 2026-10-08, 'the App Store seller shows his legal name'; app shows 'Sold by Jamin Xu (Pexi)' (app/public/js/ui-strings.js:88). Apple on expiry, https://developer.apple.com/help/account/membership/renewal/ : 'If your Apple Developer Program membership expires, your apps will no longer be available for download and you won't be able to submit new apps or updates ...' and 'However, your apps will still function for users who have already installed or downloaded them'. After a late renewal: 'Any paid apps you had available for download will become available again after you sign in to App Store Connect and accept the Paid Applications Agreement.' Auto-renew: 'If you enrolled through the Apple Developer website, you can opt in to automatic membership renewal by turning on "Auto-renew" ... only available in certain regions' (Canada is on the list). Renewal opens 30 days before expiry. Restore time is not promised: Apple's own forums carry 2026 threads of apps staying removed after renewal, e.g. https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/786108 and https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/853288 (anecdotes, not a median). Renewal date (about 2027-10-08), Auto-renew state, the card on file and Aurik's App Store Connect role are all unread (HANDOVER.md line 14 'ASSUMED a user, check'). Suspension means no new downloads, no updates, no way to move the app, but installed copies keep working; subscriptions keep billing through Apple.
fix: Read the renewal date and turn Auto-renew on; put a calendar alert 45 days before; add Aurik with an App Manager role; decide before 2027-04-01 whether to move to an organisation account (needs a legal entity and D-U-N-S, per docs/the-store-accounts-packet.md section 1a).
fix_cost: 15 minutes now; entity move is a real project
dup_of: R25, R38; new: quoted terms, installed apps keep working, restore delay evidence

evidence: Apple, https://www.developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/getting-paid/overview-of-receiving-payments : 'payments are made to the bank account and the currency you provided within 45 days' of the last day of the fiscal month; needs an active Paid Apps Agreement, banking details ('Split or multiple bank accounts aren't supported'), earnings above the threshold, and monthly invoicing where required. Threshold, https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/reference/minimum-payment-threshold : row 'CAN | Canada | CAD | 0.02', so no practical hold for Canadian accounts. A sale on day 1 of a fiscal month pays about 75 days later, a sale on the last day about 45. Cost side is paid first: Anthropic credits are prepaid and Apple's US$99 membership is yearly. launch-gaps item 22 says the agreement, both tax forms and the bank are Active (checked) while item 41 says unseen: the two disagree. Which account (personal or a business account) is not recorded in the repo; R46 lists the Ontario business registration and GST/HST steps.
fix: Record in HANDOVER.md which bank account receives Apple and whose name it is in; put the first expected payout date on the calendar; treat the first 2 to 3 months as cash going out before cash comes in.
dup_of: R26, R46, gap 41; new: CAD threshold 0.02 quoted, 45 to 75 day lag, conflicting gap 22 and 41

title: RevenueCat is a fine choice at 10,000 users; the only limits are the 1% above US$2.5K a month and a card on file
evidence: https://www.revenuecat.com/pricing/ : 'Once you reach $2.5K MTR, you'll be charged 1%.' 'No charges apply on months when you don't hit the $2.5K threshold.' 'You will be asked for credit card details on sign-up but they are optional.' and parts of the product become unavailable if no card is given at $2.5K MTR. No SLA or uptime figure on the page. Controller: Jamin's account (HANDOVER.md line 15). Failure: Plus status is looked up by the server over REST with a 10-minute 'not Plus' cache (R19, R27); during a RevenueCat outage paying shoppers are treated as free until it returns; purchases themselves still clear through Apple. 10,000 users at, say, 3% paying and CA$3.99 is about CA$1,200 a month, under the line, so RevenueCat is free at that size (assumed conversion).

dup_of: gap 70, R27, R89; new: quoted terms and the 10,000-user arithmetic

title: Anthropic: prepaid credits expire after a year and stop the API when empty; the app degrades gracefully and the cost is small
evidence: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8977456-how-do-i-pay-for-my-api-usage : 'Credits expire one year from the purchase date, and the expiration date can't be extended.' 'All credit purchases are non-refundable.' 'If you run out of credits, you can no longer call the API or use the playground until you add more.' Auto-reload 'purchases additional credits automatically when your balance falls below a threshold you set.' Spend cap, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits : Start tier monthly spend cap $500; when reached 'API usage pauses until 00:00 UTC on the first day of the next month' with HTTP 429 and no retry-after; a limit you set yourself returns HTTP 400. Haiku 5.5 is listed on the Start tier with 4,000 requests a minute, so the model name in identify/src/range-ask.ts:222 is real. App side: app/src/watch.ts:126-131 raises claude_cap_reached, claude_cap_near (80%) and claude_account_failing; shoppers get 'No price here yet' instead of a range. Ceiling on spend: the app cap is 10,000 asks a month; at the repo's own estimate of 0.23 cents per Haiku 4.5 identification (app/src/model-cost.ts:22, derived not measured, Haiku 5.5 is listed cheaper) that is about US$23 a month at most. Key owner, billing card, balance and whether auto-reload is on are unread: HANDOVER.md bills table is blank ('Jamin fills in'). Anthropic's role is a nice-to-have fallback, so a lapse costs ranges, not scans.
fix: Turn auto-reload on with a low threshold or buy credits in small amounts; calendar one alert a year for the credit expiry; fill the bills table.
fix_cost: 10 minutes, about US$25 to US$50 a year
dup_of: R34, R32; new: quoted expiry and empty-balance terms, cost ceiling, graceful fallback confirmed in code

title: Open Food Facts: the whole server shares one 15-a-minute address, so name lookups for new barcodes cap near 17,000 a day and burst misses are likely at launch
evidence: https://openfoodfacts.github.io/openfoodfacts-server/api/ : '15 req/min/IP address for all read product queries'; 'we reserve the right to deny you access to the website and the API through IP address ban'; 'If your requests come from your users directly (ex: mobile app), the rate limits apply per user' (ours do not: they leave from the Mac); 'If you expect your app to generate a lot of API traffic, we strongly encourage you to host a local instance of Product Opener'; 'The server can be temporarily unavailable'. Code: app/src/open-food-facts.ts:39-76 spaces calls 5 s apart (12 a minute, 17,280 a day at the very most), gives up after a 5 s wait and treats it as a miss; the answer cache is an in-memory Map of 2,000 entries (open-food-facts.ts:40) emptied by every restart or deploy. Only runs after the catalogue misses. At 10,000 users, if each scans 10 times a week and 15% miss the catalogue (both assumed) that is about 1.5 lookups a minute on average but evening peaks of 10 times that exceed 12 a minute and become 'no name' answers for the overflow. Same user agent now names Pexi with a contact address (checked in code).
fix: Persist learned names to the shopper data file so a barcode is asked once ever; use the OFF CSV/JSONL bulk dump (the page asks for it above a few hundred products) to widen the local catalogue so fewer scans need a live lookup.
fix_cost: half a day for persisting; the bulk import is mostly done if the catalogue already carries Open Facts rows (R82 says it does)
dup_of: R35, gap 68 (rate and user agent already fixed); new: single-address ceiling, per-user clause does not apply, cache lost on restart

title: Overpass (nearby shops): the public server's own rules say commercial use should use self-hosted or paid Overpass, and 'divide by 100' for regular use
evidence: https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Overpass_API : 'No more than 10,000 queries per day'; 'If you set something up that uses the Overpass API regularly, then divide those numbers by 100.' (that is 100 a day); 'Commercial use should use self-hosted or paid Overpass servers.'; 'Nowadays this server is overloaded - be mindful of that, do not overconsume resources and do not expect high reliability.'; 'If you receive an HTTP error code such as 429 or 406, pause for 30 seconds'. Code: app/src/stores.ts:302 default https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter, 10 s timeout, a week-long cache of up to 20,000 map squares held in a Map in memory (stores.ts around 338-346), lost at every restart or deploy; no mirror configured except SHIN_OVERPASS override. Pexi charges for Plus, so it is commercial use of a free volunteer server. Failure effect: store list empty, shoppers type prices without a shop (R77). Recovery: the next call after Overpass recovers.
fix: Point SHIN_OVERPASS at a paid or self-hosted Overpass before launch traffic, or move to a stores file built from an OSM extract of Canada (shops barely move); at minimum persist the square cache to disk.
fix_cost: 2 to 8 hours; a small paid Overpass endpoint is a few dollars to tens of dollars a month (price not checked)
dup_of: R77, gap 68 (blocking and user agent known); new: the commercial-use sentence and the 100-a-day regular-use figure

title: Project Hammer is the source of almost every shop price and is one person's website with no contract; we would not choose it as the only source for 10,000 users
evidence: mac/hammer-refresh.sh:43 downloads https://jacobfilipp.com/hammerdata/hammer-5-csv.zip. Checked 2026-11-21 22:48Z (HEAD): HTTP 200, Content-Length 548,931,390, Last-Modified 2026-11-21 22:24 UTC, Server LiteSpeed, so it is up and fresh today. Last good import on our side 2026-11-15 10:38Z (data-freshness log in the alarm run, '6.5 days ago'). launch-gaps item 34: 98,918 prices on 47,404 barcodes, 'a quarter get a shop price' (SETUP.md), so the verdicts depend on it. Availability only: if the file stops or moves, the importer refuses a bad file and keeps last week's prices (R28 checks), so shoppers see ageing prices, not an outage; if the publisher disappears there is no second source in the repo for the same retailers. Controller: an individual, no agreement, no notice period. Weekly 549 MB download from a personal host is itself a load we place on him.
fix: Keep a dated copy of each accepted file off the Mac; plan the replacement source (shopper-entered prices, a second public feed) as the long-term answer, and put a 'file not newer than 14 days' alert on.
fix_cost: 1 hour for the off-Mac copy; replacement source is product work
dup_of: R71, R28, R82; new: live availability check, 549 MB size, single-publisher concentration
